findings.source_passage: the madness of the master without the simplicity of the man would not be worth a farthing… I should like very much to know what the pair are talking about at this moment
findings.source_locator: Curate-barber dialogue after they leave Don Quixote's room
findings.why_it_matters: The curate's closing epigram — 'the madness of the master without the simplicity of the man would not be worth a farthing' — is the critical tradition's key formulation of the Don-Sancho complementarity; its absence removes interpretive ballast the chapter is famous for providing.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the curate's line verbatim or near-verbatim: 'the madness of the master without the simplicity of the man would not be worth a farthing,' along with the barber's wish to overhear them and the curate's remark that the niece or housekeeper will report.

findings.source_passage: if the naked truth, undisguised by flattery, came to the ears of princes, times would be different, and other ages would be reckoned iron ages more than ours, which I hold to be the golden of these latter days
findings.source_locator: Don Quixote's speech requesting Sancho's report, mid-segment
findings.why_it_matters: Don Quixote's meditation on princes, flattery, and the golden age is thematically loaded — it ironically echoes his earlier golden-age speech and carries distinctive Cervantine political irony; erasing it flattens his speech to a bare request.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the core formulation about naked truth and princes, and the 'golden of these latter days' clause, as they are interpretively distinctive and tonally signature.

findings.source_passage: you bag of mischief and sack of knavery; go govern your house and dig your seed-patch, and give over looking for islands or shylands
findings.source_locator: Housekeeper's speech, first exchange at the door
findings.why_it_matters: The housekeeper's insult 'bag of mischief and sack of knavery' is the rhetorically distinctive moment of the opening exchange; the draft drops the first half, keeping only the milder instruction, losing the comic energy of the double-insult.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'bag of mischief and sack of knavery' before 'go govern thy house.'

findings.source_passage: That's just where it is, body of my father! … There's the tail to be skinned yet; all so far is cakes and fancy bread
findings.source_locator: Sancho's exclamation before naming Carrasco, late segment
findings.why_it_matters: Sancho's 'cakes and fancy bread' idiom and the 'body of my father' oath are voice-establishing register markers; the draft preserves 'tail to be skinned yet' but drops both colorful idioms, slightly flattening Sancho's distinctive speech.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'body of my father' and 'all so far is cakes and fancy bread' to preserve Sancho's proverbial register.

summary: The draft loses the curate's critical epigram on the master-man complementarity and Don Quixote's politically ironic speech on flattery and princes — two passages of high interpretive and voice weight — triggering a regenerate verdict on medium-severity grounds.
